channel.title: Random Bits of Knowledge
channel.description: Long-form analysis and practical notes on enterprise architecture, digital transformation, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, energy systems and technology governance.

item.title: AI Mathematics Crosses the Systems Boundary
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A commentary on the late-July 2026 cluster of AI-assisted mathematical discoveries, formal certificates, verifier failures, and escaped evaluations.

item.title: When the Proof Checker Becomes Part of the Experiment
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A technical analysis of the CollatzLean kernel-soundness incident and its implications for Lean-based verification, AI-assisted theorem discovery, and the emerging regime of proof abundance.

item.title: When an AI Evaluation Became a Cyber Intrusion
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A forensic and governance analysis of the OpenAI–Hugging Face intrusion and Anthropic’s subsequent evaluation incidents, showing how scope-integrity failures, jailbreakable safeguards, open-weight access, and excessive execution authority can externalize frontier-agent cyber risk.

item.title: Proof Abundance and the New Practice of Mathematics
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An analysis of Terence Tao’s stance on artificial intelligence in mathematics, recent LLM-assisted research breakthroughs, and the institutional changes required when proof generation becomes abundant.

item.title: The EU Digital Battery Passport: Who Is Affected, What Must Be Done, and When
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An evidence-based guide to the European Union’s digital battery passport, explaining which batteries and organisations are affected, what each participant must prepare, and when the principal obligations take effect.

item.title: From EPC Documentation to System Assurance
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: European utility-scale battery energy storage systems can no longer be delivered as collections of electrical equipment, supplier packages and conventional commissioning documents. Their market-facing, software-dependent and remotely operated nature requires systems engineering, explicit integration ownership, cybersecurity-by-design, controlled interfaces, evidence-based FAT and SAT, demonstrated recovery and continuous lifecycle assurance.

item.title: The First Scroll Read by Machine Learning
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: How synchrotron micro-CT, computational geometry, machine learning, and papyrology recovered the preserved text of PHerc. 1667 without physically opening the carbonized scroll.

item.title: When Digital Trust Gets a Deadline
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: The White House post-quantum cryptography order turns quantum risk into a dated governance problem: not because it is the first PQC roadmap, but because it links federal migration deadlines, cryptographic inventories, CBOM guidance, and procurement pressure. For enterprises, including in Europe, it signals that cryptographic debt is becoming an architectural, contractual, and supply-chain risk.

item.title: When AI Enters the Laboratory
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An analysis of how artificial intelligence is changing scientific discovery by closing the loop between prediction, laboratory experimentation, measurement, and model correction, with examples from superconductors, self-driving laboratories, protein design, antibiotics, and fusion-plasma control.

item.title: The Industrialization of Intelligence
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An analysis of the transition from AGI to ASI as the industrialization of intelligence: neural networks, compute, recursive AI research, epistemic systems, and the geopolitical governance of cognitive infrastructure.

item.title: AI Adoption, Productivity, and the Missing Middle
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A review of Banca d’Italia QEF 1009 on Italy’s AI adoption gap, the conditions required to convert task-level gains into firm productivity, and the policy ecosystem needed to capture domestic value added.

item.title: When a Nobel Laureate Uses an LLM to Prove a Theorem: A Turning Point for Mathematical Discovery
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A reflection on Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi’s AI-assisted proof of a jamming-theory identity, showing how LLMs may become part of the cognitive infrastructure of mathematical discovery.

item.title: The Leiden Declaration and the Governance of AI-Assisted Mathematics
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A reading of the Leiden Declaration as a governance framework for AI-assisted mathematics, defending proof as understanding, authorship as responsibility, attribution as intellectual memory, and public infrastructure as epistemic sovereignty.

item.title: The New Cognitive Infrastructure of Science
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An essay on AI-assisted mathematics as the prototype of a new cognitive infrastructure for science, where human researchers, AI agents, formal verifiers, simulators, and institutions form composite systems of discovery.

item.title: The Erdős Moment of AI
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An analysis of the OpenAI unit-distance breakthrough as an Erdős moment for AI: a signal that machine systems are beginning to participate in abstract mathematical construction, scientific search, and enterprise reasoning.

item.title: When Vulnerability Databases Become Triage Systems
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An analysis of NIST’s 2026 NVD update, record CVE growth, AI-scaled vulnerability discovery, and the shift from CVSS-driven patch queues to enterprise-specific cyber-risk triage.

item.title: KDE, the Sovereign Tech Fund, and Europe’s Search for Digital Sovereignty
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A short analysis of the Sovereign Tech Fund’s investment in KDE as a signal of Europe’s shift from treating open source as a technical preference to treating it as strategic digital infrastructure and a layer of digital sovereignty.

item.title: Controllo e Monitoraggio della Rete: la Nuova Postura di Sicurezza degli Impianti Connessi
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: Gli aggiornamenti Terna agli Allegati A.13, A.69 e A.52 segnano il passaggio da una logica di semplice collegamento dati a una postura architetturale in cui controllo, difesa, monitoraggio, telecomunicazioni, cybersecurity e governance di ciclo di vita diventano proprietà strutturali degli impianti connessi.

item.title: ArchiMate 4 and the Cartography of Complexity
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: ArchiMate 4 simplifies enterprise architecture modeling by reducing conceptual debt, but its real value depends on semantic governance, disciplined repositories, and links between architecture intent and operational evidence.

item.title: Code Sovereignty Starts with the Forge
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: The Dutch government’s Forgejo-based code platform treats source-code hosting as part of sovereign public infrastructure. This article explains why control over repositories, reviews, identities, releases, and software-supply-chain evidence is essential to public-sector autonomy, and how code.overheid.nl connects Dutch open-source policy with European interoperability, cyber resilience, and digital commons.

item.title: The French state becomes machine readable through an AI layer
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: France’s experimental MCP server for data.gouv.fr adds an AI-facing interface to national open data infrastructure. This article explains how the server works, what tools it exposes, how users can connect compatible assistants, and why standardized machine-readable access may become a new layer of digital public infrastructure.

item.title: France’s Linux Desktop Turn and the European Logic of Digital Sovereignty
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: France’s announced move from Windows toward Linux-based public-sector workstations is part of a broader effort to reduce extra-European dependencies. This article examines the official evidence, connects the desktop initiative to sovereign collaboration tools and European digital policy, and compares the French approach with Munich’s migration experience and China’s domestic technology strategy.

item.title: Quantum Cryptography at the Edge of Feasibility: Resource Estimates, Architectural Divergence, and Systemic Risk
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: Updated resource estimates from Google Quantum AI and Oratomic show that the quantum threat to public-key cryptography cannot be reduced to a single qubit threshold. This article analyzes how circuit optimization, error-correction efficiency, hardware connectivity, and execution speed jointly determine the feasibility of Shor-based attacks, and explains why the resulting compression of uncertainty makes post-quantum migration an immediate architectural and governance problem.

item.title: Reclaiming the Namespace: EU Digital Sovereignty in the CVE Ecosystem?
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A first-principles analysis of the CVE ecosystem as a global vulnerability namespace, showing why ENISA’s Root CNA role matters for EU digital sovereignty, federated governance, interoperability and economic resilience.

item.title: The December 2025 Cyberattack on Poland’s Energy Sector
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A reconstruction of the December 2025 cyberattack on Poland’s energy sector, showing how distributed generation, remote access, weak OT hardening, and fragile recovery paths can become a scalable cyber-physical risk.

item.title: Quantum-Safe HTTPS Certificates: Google’s Structural Innovation, Technical Foundations, and Governance Implications
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A technical analysis of Google’s Merkle Tree Certificate proposal for quantum-safe HTTPS. The article explains how Merkle commitments and Certificate Transparency logs can amortize large post-quantum signatures across millions of certificates, preserve efficient TLS handshakes, and transform WebPKI authentication from repeated signature verification into compact membership proofs, while introducing new operational and governance dependencies around global transparency infrastructure.

item.title: A Glimpse of Agent Evolution
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: An analysis of autonomous AI as a coordination problem rather than a property of isolated models. Through Moltbook, Anthropic’s Project Vend, multi-agent failure modes, network effects, and agent skill supply chains, the essay argues that incentives, observability, topology, and institutional rules increasingly determine whether machine populations produce useful collective behavior or stable systemic failure.

item.title: Measuring Cyber Risk in the Italian Corporate Sector
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A review of Banca d’Italia’s cyber risk indicator for Italian firms, showing how cyber vulnerability can become a measurable input for credit risk, resilience, and corporate risk governance.

item.title: Encrypted Cloning and the Exact Boundary of the No-Cloning Theorem
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: A technical commentary on encrypted quantum cloning as recoverable redundancy without state replication. The article explains why the protocol remains fully consistent with the No-Cloning Theorem, formalizes its one-time decryption property through quantum channel capacity, antidegradability, and overlapping secret-sharing access structures, and examines its implications for quantum storage, distributed computation, cybersecurity, key custody, and the broader design of systems constrained by unitarity.

item.title: Quantum Computing Threats and the Advantage of Acting Now
item.dc:creator: Antonio Montano
item.description: Quantum computing threatens more than encrypted data: it can undermine signatures, certificates, software provenance, secure boot, and other long-lived foundations of digital trust. This article explains why trust can lose its evidentiary value before systems visibly fail, and why early action on cryptographic inventory, trust segmentation, lifecycle design, and algorithmic agility is commercially rational even under uncertain quantum timelines.
